display.purpose: Marketing heroes on larecipe-docs. Never inside a docs page. 56px / 600 / -0.04em.

h2.purpose: Sections; feed the TOC and search records. 24px / 600 / -0.02em.

lead.purpose: Page description under the H1, ink muted, max 640px.

label.purpose: JetBrains Mono 11px / 500 / 0.1em uppercase: nav groups, ticket headers, code titles.

meta.purpose: JetBrains Mono 11.5px: provenance, paths, hashes, reading time.

code.purpose: JetBrains Mono 13.5px / 1.7 on the dark slab.

shadows.name: ring-focus

motion.name: duration-state

motion.name: duration-panel

themeTokens.description: What a team may override in larecipe.json `theme`. Everything else is structure.
themeTokens.accent: Replaces violet. Soft and dark variants are derived in OKLCH; contrast is validated by larecipe:validate.
themeTokens.fonts: sans, mono, arabic stacks; Google Fonts or self-hosted files in the docs root.
themeTokens.provenance: true (default) shows updated-by lines and the Last change ticket.

narrative.overview: In a restaurant kitchen, the pass is the counter where every plate is checked before it leaves. LaRecipe is that counter for documentation: code changes fire tickets, agents prepare the docs, a human signs them off, and the reader receives a page that says exactly when and why it changed. Paper and ink, one violet for state, mono for what machines produced, a clean sans for what people read, and the ticket (perforated header, bitten edge) as the signature shape. Light and dark are first-class; Arabic is a peer rendering.
keyCharacteristics: Paper and ink first; violet is a state, never a decoration.
Mono for what machines produced; sans for what people read.
The ticket is the signature shape.
Provenance is designed into the page.
Flat at rest; shadows only on floating surfaces.
Motion is mechanical and exact (120 / 180 / 240 ms).

rules.name: The Violet-Is-State Rule
rules.body: Violet means active, focused, selected, linked, fresh or the single primary action. One filled violet button per screen. The mark is never violet.

rules.name: The Labels-Not-Washes Rule
rules.body: Callouts, badges and alerts get meaning from a colored label and icon on a neutral surface. No tinted fills, no side stripes.

rules.name: The Measured-Ink Rule
rules.body: Text uses the alpha ladder 0.92 / 0.66 / 0.44. Information never sits at the faint step.

rules.name: The Customer-Accent Rule
rules.body: A team's accent replaces violet through tokens with derived variants. Structure and signature elements stay; LaRecipe's mark appears only as an optional credit.

rules.name: The Firm-Heading Rule
rules.body: Docs headings ship at 600 with negative tracking because readers scan docs before they read them.

rules.name: The Machine-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Paths, hashes, commands, timestamps, ticket numbers, shortcuts and version ids are mono. Human writing is sans.

rules.name: The Arabic-Breathes Rule
rules.body: Arabic never inherits negative tracking, runs prose at 1.8, maps 600 to Thmanyah 700, and turns mono labels into sans 500.

rules.name: The Numerals-Stay-LTR Rule
rules.body: Inside RTL, numerals, versions, hashes and commands stay left to right.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards, callouts, tickets and code blocks have no shadow at rest or on hover. Hover is a stronger hairline.

rules.name: The Shared-Canvas Rule
rules.body: Header, sidebar, article and TOC share the canvas; boundaries are one hairline.

dos: Do keep violet for state: focus, selection, the active page, links, freshness and the one primary action.
Do set machine-made things in mono and human writing in sans.
Do show provenance on every page.
Do carry structure with whitespace, the hairline and the perforation before reaching for a box.
Do keep corners at 4, 6 or 10 px.
Do check every surface in light, dark, LTR, RTL and with JavaScript disabled.
Do keep code and numerals left to right inside RTL.
Do consume icons through one Icons namespace (Lucide, 1.75 stroke).
Do let a team's accent, fonts and logo replace LaRecipe's on their docs.
donts: Don't use gradients, glassmorphism, sparkles or neon.
Don't tint callouts or add colored side stripes.
Don't put more than one filled violet button on a screen.
Don't draw the mark in violet.
Don't add shadows to cards, callouts, tickets or code blocks.
Don't use pure black or white for text, or information at the faint step.
Don't float a chat bubble over the content.
Don't use kitchen slang on customer docs by default.
Don't use em dashes in copy.
